dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: CALM CORRIDOR / VEIL MARKET

dialogueInline.speaker: SURVEY OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Captain, I have a question about the aft camera.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: If it's about the grease on the housing, the technician has already promised to clean it.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Why is the navigation star behind us also ahead of us?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: Which one is a reflection?

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: I hoped you'd tell me.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: Don't do that. Tell me what you measured.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Optics, ranging and passive field return agree. Same spectrum. Same drift. It moves when we alter attitude, only less than it should. There are two returns, and every timing beacon says we're exactly where we were supposed to be.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: You've checked the independent clock?

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Three times.

panelPlan: THE LATTICE. A survey ship proceeds through the Calm Corridor, a route whose instruments have been boringly reliable. Its captain has arranged her life around.
The captain stops writing. She approaches the console, looking first at the officer, then the feed.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *THE LATTICE. A survey ship proceeds through the Calm Corridor, a route whose instruments have been boringly reliable. Its captain has arranged her life around boring instruments. A junior survey officer discovers a star duplicated in two contradictory directions. It isn't marked on any of the overlays.*
*The captain stops writing. She approaches the console, looking first at the officer, then the feed.*

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: Check it again.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Do you want a different answer?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: Desperately. But I'll settle for a true one.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: That wasn't on the earlier pass.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: How fast is it moving relative to us?

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: That's the problem. The optical position says it's ahead. The range return says it never left the volume behind us.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: And our actual separation from the nearest anchor?

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Stable.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: Very good. We have one fact that can still be trusted. Reduce speed. I want an independent position check from the next beacon and a complete record on an isolated circuit.

panelPlan: He checks. The ship's clocks agree to the tolerance they had before the departure. A second duplicate appears, a faint reflection of an old probe at the edge.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *He checks. The ship's clocks agree to the tolerance they had before the departure. A second duplicate appears, a faint reflection of an old probe at the edge of the passage.*

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Shall I report an unsafe corridor?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: Report an unexplained observation inside a corridor whose verified measurements remain in tolerance. Don't tell people they're safe on the strength of a number that has just made a fool of us. Don't tell them they're doomed either.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: My father travels this route next week.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: Then let's give him something better than a story about a second star.

panelPlan: The officer begins the transmission. A long pause passes while they watch the duplicated star. Both know that the most alarming thing is not that their system.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *The officer begins the transmission. A long pause passes while they watch the duplicated star. Both know that the most alarming thing is not that their system has failed. It is that the system hasn't failed in any measurable way.*

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: VEIL MARKET

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Do you know what the first man asked me? Whether the duplicated star was worth the cost of the ticket. As though I were selling tickets to a view.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: You sell guarantees.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Of windows. Timing. Where a freighter can be without being sheared apart. I have never guaranteed the astronomical objects will behave themselves for the passengers.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: You've guaranteed a safe arrival based on the clocks. The clocks are giving us a reading that doesn't fit what the cameras can see.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: The clocks have been independently checked.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: That's why I'm not sleeping.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I could sell a warning. Narrow the next window, charge a premium, tell people we're taking special precautions.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Are we?

panelPlan: VEIL MARKET. Naomi is at Jex's broker table with the unedited survey records. His customers have already heard three versions of the anomaly, including one.
He takes the record from her and scans it. For once, the numbers tell him nothing useful.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *VEIL MARKET. Naomi is at Jex's broker table with the unedited survey records. His customers have already heard three versions of the anomaly, including one that involves a ship with no crew.*
*He takes the record from her and scans it. For once, the numbers tell him nothing useful.*
sourceScene: SCENE 2 — THE COST OF BEING CERTAIN (P03–P04)

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: No. I said I could sell one.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Then you should be ashamed of yourself.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I am. I'm also trying to understand what happens to this market when every trader decides the roads have gone mad. Both feelings are available to me.

dialogueInline.speaker: JIA
dialogueInline.text: The sensor arrays aren't disagreeing. They're reporting phase-repeated returns within the verified volume. I can quantify the offset. I cannot tell you why it happens.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Can it move a ship?

dialogueInline.speaker: JIA
dialogueInline.text: I have no evidence it has moved any mass at all.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Good. Then I'm not ordering anyone to shoot a reflection until you've decided whether it can shoot back.

panelPlan: On THUNDERBREAK, Jia Morgan works at a measured field display. Selene Stormwell has brought old logs. Venn and Deka arrive from separate workstations, neither.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *On THUNDERBREAK, Jia Morgan works at a measured field display. Selene Stormwell has brought old logs. Venn and Deka arrive from separate workstations, neither pretending the ship has gained a second captain.*
sourceScene: SCENE 2 — THE COST OF BEING CERTAIN (P03–P04)

dialogueInline.speaker: SELENE
dialogueInline.text: There are older Academy records of vessels appearing beside themselves near lost anchors. Entire crews wrote accounts. They couldn't all have imagined it.

dialogueInline.speaker: JIA
dialogueInline.text: They may have seen something. They didn't have instruments that could separate an optical return from a real target. If you ask me to use the records as a warning, yes. If you ask me to use them as measurements, no.

dialogueInline.speaker: SELENE
dialogueInline.text: There was a time when people called the Shattering an error in their maps.

dialogueInline.speaker: JIA
dialogueInline.text: And there was a time when people called infection a punishment. Historical descriptions are evidence that someone observed a problem, not evidence that their explanation was right.

panelPlan: Selene looks wounded, but not because the scientific point is wrong.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Selene looks wounded, but not because the scientific point is wrong.*
sourceScene: SCENE 2 — THE COST OF BEING CERTAIN (P03–P04)

dialogueInline.speaker: SELENE
dialogueInline.text: I'm not asking you to believe the explanation. I'm asking you not to throw away the observation because it comes from frightened people who didn't have your equipment.

dialogueInline.speaker: JIA
dialogueInline.text: That is fair. Give me their raw descriptions. I'll keep the interpretations separate.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Good. I need a working restriction, not an argument about who deserves to be right. What can our escorts do differently today?

dialogueInline.speaker: JIA
dialogueInline.text: Stop mirroring their course changes until I know whether synchronous inputs alter the effect.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Fine by me. They were making formation flying far too fashionable.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Commodore, the Admiralty has confirmed your temporary field appointment. You will coordinate Fleet assets in the corridor. Lieutenant Deka remains in command of Thunderbreak. The tribunal finding stands.

panelPlan: Jia stops, considering that.
Dominion appears on the command channel. He can hear only the professional end of an argument that has been going on for some time.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Jia stops, considering that.*
*Dominion appears on the command channel. He can hear only the professional end of an argument that has been going on for some time.*
sourceScene: SCENE 2 — THE COST OF BEING CERTAIN (P03–P04)

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Understood.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: I should hope so. I only just got the chair adjusted.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Lieutenant, I don't imagine you need reminding what this means.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Not unless there's something new in it.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Very well. Use your judgment. And record it.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I haven't come back for the chair.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: I know. I didn't expect you to. It's the rest of the ship that worries me. When I give an order, half the crew still looks to see whether you approve.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I'll speak to them.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Don't. Let me. They're my crew now, and I need them to understand that before we have to do something ugly.

panelPlan: The channel closes. Venn stays beside Deka for a moment.
Venn accepts the correction. Deka is pleased, but doesn't turn it into a ceremony. Behind them Jia starts drafting a test.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *The channel closes. Venn stays beside Deka for a moment.*
*Venn accepts the correction. Deka is pleased, but doesn't turn it into a ceremony. Behind them Jia starts drafting a test.*
sourceScene: SCENE 2 — THE COST OF BEING CERTAIN (P03–P04)

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: TAL CORVUS / ASHFANG — SURVEY DISCUSSION

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: If you touch that before the pressure crew gets here, I'm going to tell your supervisor you fell into it trying to impress me.

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: I wasn't trying to impress you.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Then you have even less excuse.

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: People are saying the corridors are making copies of us.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: People said my radiator repair was finished last month. People say all sorts of things.

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: Are you frightened?

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Yes. I'm frightened of the pressure reading changing after I've put people through the next door. I'm frightened of a child getting curious while I stand here talking to you. Those I can do something about. Go get the rope barrier.

panelPlan: The Tal Corvus service passage has been closed because a thin physical seep has formed on a structural seam. Tess has been asked to look at it. A maintenance.
The worker does. Tess waits, watching the seam without claiming it is alive or aware.
On ASHFANG, Billie watches the footage in sour silence. Her officer has seen her do something reckless before and is prepared for it.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *The Tal Corvus service passage has been closed because a thin physical seep has formed on a structural seam. Tess has been asked to look at it. A maintenance worker keeps leaning toward the phenomenon, attracted by the way the light seems doubled along its edge.*
*Tess crouches to examine the seam, but keeps her hands off it.*
*The worker does. Tess waits, watching the seam without claiming it is alive or aware.*
*On ASHFANG, Billie watches the footage in sour silence. Her officer has seen her do something reckless before and is prepared for it.*
sourceScene: SCENE 3 — WHO GETS TO BE FRIGHTENED (P05–P07)

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: If there's a second ship out there, what happens if we fire on it?

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: We don't know there is a second ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: That's why I asked.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: We also don't know whether weapons will affect whatever the return is. We'd be firing through the same volume the civilian craft use.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Am I ordering you to load a gun?

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: No.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Then I'm permitted to wonder aloud. I know everyone has forgotten it, but I used to be allowed that on my own bridge.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Who made this version?

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: It came from the Arena Vault.

panelPlan: She switches off the most dramatic piece of footage. It had been cut to repeat the moment of apparent duplication.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *She switches off the most dramatic piece of footage. It had been cut to repeat the moment of apparent duplication.*
sourceScene: SCENE 3 — WHO GETS TO BE FRIGHTENED (P05–P07)

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Naturally. Nothing travels faster than something that might frighten somebody.

dialogueInline.speaker: EMISSARY
dialogueInline.text: The uncut report says the transit measurements remain within tolerance. If we distribute only the images, anyone who sees the original will know we've removed the context.

dialogueInline.speaker: FEAR MASK
dialogueInline.text: They may. Many won't wait for context before refusing to travel.

dialogueInline.speaker: EMISSARY
dialogueInline.text: You want the corridor shut?

dialogueInline.speaker: FEAR MASK
dialogueInline.text: I want the pilots to ask us whether to enter it. Today the pilots have their own instruments and their own witnesses. Tomorrow they may require reassurance from an authority who knows what to show them.

dialogueInline.speaker: EMISSARY
dialogueInline.text: And if the anomaly is harmless?

dialogueInline.speaker: FEAR MASK
dialogueInline.text: Then they'll be relieved. Relief is a powerful thing to supply to someone you've frightened.

panelPlan: In the ARENA VAULT, the Fear Mask watches the same clip. Its emissary has the original transmission, complete with the survey captain's uncertainty.
The emissary doesn't share the Mask's satisfaction. He has relatives traveling through that corridor. He asks for the uncut feed to be retained in the official.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *In the ARENA VAULT, the Fear Mask watches the same clip. Its emissary has the original transmission, complete with the survey captain's uncertainty.*
*The emissary doesn't share the Mask's satisfaction. He has relatives traveling through that corridor. He asks for the uncut feed to be retained in the official archive and gets no reply.*
sourceScene: SCENE 3 — WHO GETS TO BE FRIGHTENED (P05–P07)

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: CALM CORRIDOR — SUNLASH / GRAVEFIRE

dialogueInline.speaker: SECOND
dialogueInline.text: Naomi, there's a second Gravefire on our starboard optical feed.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Does it have a second Tess? Because one of them could take a shift.

dialogueInline.speaker: SECOND
dialogueInline.text: One transponder. Two returns. The second return appears to be answering the primary before it receives the signal.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Tess. Tell me what you see. Don't tell me what you think it is.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: My ship. From an angle nobody should be able to see it. And somebody's fixed the radiator on the reflection. Very poor attention to detail.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Is your hull pressure steady?

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: All normal. Cooling's still a problem. We are making no move toward the other ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Good.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: You were going to say that without asking me, weren't you?

panelPlan: Sunlash leads a mixed civilian convoy into the Calm Corridor. Gravefire escorts the rear. The first echoed ship appears beside Tess's cutter. It has the same.
Naomi stops smiling. She changes attitude slightly and watches the real escort respond.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Sunlash leads a mixed civilian convoy into the Calm Corridor. Gravefire escorts the rear. The first echoed ship appears beside Tess's cutter. It has the same damaged radiator housing, the same hull markings and a tiny lag in its attitude change. It looks almost real enough to make a pilot want to salute it.*
*Naomi stops smiling. She changes attitude slightly and watches the real escort respond.*

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: I was. I know it's rude.

dialogueInline.speaker: FREIGHTER PILOT
dialogueInline.text: I've got Gravefire crossing my bow. I'll follow its turn.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: No. You have a return that looks like Gravefire. The real one is behind you, and I've never steered you into a wall before. Keep your course.

dialogueInline.speaker: FREIGHTER PILOT
dialogueInline.text: The other one looks closer.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Close your forward visual if you have to. Use the instruments we verified at the last anchor. You don't have to like the view.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Your last course correction was good. Give me that exact turn back, slowly. You're not being asked to trust the whole universe. You're being asked to keep one ship in one measured lane.

dialogueInline.speaker: FREIGHTER PILOT
dialogueInline.text: I have children aboard.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: I know. Let's get them home without teaching them to fly by chasing pictures.

panelPlan: An inexperienced civilian captain turns toward the bright duplicate, believing it marks the safe escort path. His freighter begins to deviate from the verified.
The pilot manages the turn. The visual echo drifts across the canopy and becomes more vivid, as though inviting a second correction. He holds course.
The pilot says nothing further. Tess watches his freighter regain the verified course while the second Gravefire lingers impossibly beside the first.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *An inexperienced civilian captain turns toward the bright duplicate, believing it marks the safe escort path. His freighter begins to deviate from the verified volume.*
*His hands tremble at the controls. Naomi can hear breathing over the open circuit.*
*The pilot manages the turn. The visual echo drifts across the canopy and becomes more vivid, as though inviting a second correction. He holds course.*
*The pilot says nothing further. Tess watches his freighter regain the verified course while the second Gravefire lingers impossibly beside the first.*

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: THUNDERBREAK

dialogueInline.speaker: JIA
dialogueInline.text: There's a pattern. When the ships repeat one another's corrections at nearly identical intervals, the echoes become more coherent. We can see a relationship. We haven't proved the field's mechanism.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Does that relationship survive different instruments?

dialogueInline.speaker: JIA
dialogueInline.text: Yes. Not all of the measurements have the same precision, but the tendency survives.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: If we stop making corrections together, what happens to the escorts? They're trained to keep that formation.

dialogueInline.speaker: JIA
dialogueInline.text: I believe the echo coherence will decline.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Believe, or know?

dialogueInline.speaker: JIA
dialogueInline.text: Believe. I would rather be wrong in a way we can measure than certain in a way that gets someone killed.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: We can't pause the convoy for a laboratory experiment.

panelPlan: THUNDERBREAK. Jia has grouped every recorded course adjustment, firing impulse and timing input. Venn asks to see only the observations relevant to the convoy.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *THUNDERBREAK. Jia has grouped every recorded course adjustment, firing impulse and timing input. Venn asks to see only the observations relevant to the convoy currently in the corridor.*

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: We can make the convoy the experiment. I know the spacing margins. I can vary the freighters' turns and arrival intervals without losing the safe volume.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: You're going to ask merchant captains to abandon the escort pattern while a second copy of their ship stares at them.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Yes. I'm not delighted about it either.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Then tell them why. Don't give them the word 'desynchronization' and expect it to keep them calm.

panelPlan: Venn opens the civilian circuit. She starts formally, then stops. The pilot's breathing can be heard over Naomi's channel.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Venn opens the civilian circuit. She starts formally, then stops. The pilot's breathing can be heard over Naomi's channel.*

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Your escorts have a proposed maneuver. It changes the formation you were told to trust. The corridor remains within the measured transit boundary, but we are seeing duplicated returns we cannot yet explain. Captain Sol will give you individual directions. Do not mirror the ship ahead of you unless she specifically tells you to.

dialogueInline.speaker: FREIGHTER PILOT
dialogueInline.text: Is something about to hit us?

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Nothing we've measured suggests a second physical vessel is approaching you. We are changing the flight pattern because the existing one appears to make the echoes worse.

dialogueInline.speaker: FREIGHTER PILOT
dialogueInline.text: That's not very comforting.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: No. It isn't. But it's what we know.

panelPlan: Jia glances up. Venn doesn't answer until she has a useful distinction.
Deka turns toward her tactical crew.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Jia glances up. Venn doesn't answer until she has a useful distinction.*
*Deka turns toward her tactical crew.*

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Cancel synchronized fire triggers. Independent defensive authority only. No shooting because the ship beside us shot at a shape. If someone has an actual physical target, I'll hear it from the officer responsible.

dialogueInline.speaker: TACTICAL
dialogueInline.text: Captain, we may lose a firing opportunity.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: I am prepared to miss a ghost. I am not prepared to put a round through a freighter because a ghost looked convincing.

dialogueInline.speaker: FREIGHTER PILOT
dialogueInline.text: Sunlash, we're losing our escort geometry.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: I know. That's deliberate. You've still got your safe corridor and you've still got us. You're allowed to hate this maneuver while you're doing it.

dialogueInline.speaker: FREIGHTER PILOT
dialogueInline.text: I already do.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Then we're ahead of schedule.

dialogueInline.speaker: JIA
dialogueInline.text: Coherence is falling. Timing inputs remain valid. This is the response I predicted.

panelPlan: One of the officers hesitates.
Naomi begins splitting the convoy deliberately. Each pilot receives a different speed and attitude instruction. Tess takes the trailing ship in hand.
The echo behind Gravefire begins to blur. The bright duplicate appears to move out of phase, then breaks into ordinary reflections. Jia watches the readings.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *One of the officers hesitates.*

*Naomi begins splitting the convoy deliberately. Each pilot receives a different speed and attitude instruction. Tess takes the trailing ship in hand while keeping Gravefire within its limited cooling margin. From the outside, it looks disorderly. To people accustomed to elegant formations, it looks like a mistake.*
*The echo behind Gravefire begins to blur. The bright duplicate appears to move out of phase, then breaks into ordinary reflections. Jia watches the readings rather than the imagery.*

dialogueInline.speaker: SELENE
dialogueInline.text: Does it tell us why the original measurements stayed healthy?

dialogueInline.speaker: JIA
dialogueInline.text: No. It tells us we can influence a phenomenon we still don't understand. That's not a small thing. It's also not an explanation.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Log the procedure and the uncertainty. The next convoy deserves both.

panelPlan: Venn watches the last freighter make the unsynchronized turn.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Venn watches the last freighter make the unsynchronized turn.*

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: VEIL MARKET

dialogueInline.speaker: BUYER
dialogueInline.text: I don't need a lecture about phase. I need a private forecast of which windows to take.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: The most honest forecast is the public survey report. It gives the verified measurements and explains what we don't know.

dialogueInline.speaker: BUYER
dialogueInline.text: I can read a public report myself.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Congratulations. You're already receiving better service than half my customers.

dialogueInline.speaker: BUYER
dialogueInline.text: I pay to know before the others.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I can sell you earlier notice of a real change in the window when one has been measured. I can't sell you the power to make a passage behave differently for your ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: BUYER
dialogueInline.text: Other brokers will.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Yes. Some of them will be wrong for less money. I've never understood why that improves the bargain.

panelPlan: VEIL MARKET. Jex has a customer demanding an exclusive alert service. The buyer has enough money to pay more than an entire relief crew earns in a season. Jex.

dialogueInline.text: The footage contradicts our warning that the corridor was unusable. It has already been copied beyond the city.

dialogueInline.text: Learn who relies on them. A courier doesn't have to be believed by everyone. Only by the people who expect them to arrive with the next correction.
